newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian shares finish at record closing high.
newsitem.headline: Australian shares finish at record closing high.

text.p: The Australian share market climbed to a record close on Monday with market sentiment buoyed by a Wall Street rally on Friday and a A$2.65 billion merger proposal between two regional banks.
The key share market barometer, the All Ordinaries index ended 26.5 points higher at 2,363.3, three points lower than the intra-day and all time high of 2,366.3 set in afternoon trade.
The previous intra-day high was 2,350.4 on February 3, 1994, and the record closing high was 2,340.6 on the same day.
The December share price index finished up 32 points at 2,391 and at a 27.7 point premium to the underlying index.
Brokers early gains were spread evenly but major resource issues BHP, WMC and CRA pulled the market higher in late trade.

"There is a weight of money looking for good industrial stocks and the indications are that our market is not overvalued in the current low interest rate and low inflation rate environment," said Rob Black, a senior dealer at Perth brokerage, Hartley Poynton.
Black said most bad news was behind the market and with mostly better news ahead, the Australian market looked set to rise in the medium to longer term.
Dealers said one factor aiding the resources sector was market speculation that commodity prices were currently at or close to lows, especially prices for aluminium and copper.

Market interest centred on banks with regionals St George and Advance announcing a merger proposal under which St George would offer A$7.30 (US$5.77) per Advance share. When the two banks' shares restarted trade just after midday, St George slumped while Advance shares jumped towards the offer price.
Benefiting the most from the merger announcement were regionals, Bank of Melbourne and Adelaide Bank, which dealers said were the most attractive of the remaining regional banks.
ANZ Bank also had a stronger session, with dealers saying the bank's stock recovered from being sold on Friday on market speculation it would make an offer for Advance.
